hints.title: Interval End Coordinate Alignment
hints.text: An arrow shoots through all balloons whose intervals overlap at that coordinate. What interval sorting strategy allows shooting as many overlapping balloons as possible?

hints.title: Earliest End Coordinate Arrow Invariant
hints.text: Sorting intervals by end coordinate ensures shooting an arrow at the earliest ending point pops all currently overlapping intervals greedily.

hints.title: Greedy Interval End Scanning Procedure
hints.text: Sort balloons by their end positions. Set arrow position to the end of the first balloon and initialize arrow count to 1. For each subsequent balloon, if its start position exceeds the current arrow position, fire a new arrow at its end and increment arrow count.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: input array length or bit count
complexity.notes: Optimal solution achieving O(N log N) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Testing all possible coordinate placements across continuous ranges takes unbounded time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Sorting intervals by endpoint takes O(N log N) time and enables an O(N) single-pass greedy scan with O(1) extra space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should sort strictly by end coordinate and handle integer overflow when comparing coordinates (e.g. avoiding x[1] - y[1] in Java/C++).
